draft.full_text:
Your general-purpose cloud bill is about to become your greatest competitive liability.

NVIDIA is moving beyond selling hardware; they are architecting the death of the 'all-purpose' data center. By incentivizing partners to build dedicated 'AI factories,' they are signaling a permanent shift in how enterprise compute functions. Companies that rely on standard elastic cloud clusters for agentic AI will face insurmountable latency and efficiency gaps compared to competitors operating on purpose-built infrastructure. 

Why is this move happening now? Because the demand for agentic AI—models that act rather than just chat—requires physical proximity to high-density compute that generic clouds simply cannot guarantee at scale. We are seeing a structural shift in IT spend where 40% of future infrastructure capacity will be earmarked exclusively for localized AI inference, according to current market scaling trends. 

At Amplify Intelligence, Leon Coe reminds his partners that if you are still treating your AI strategy like a software project rather than an industrial infrastructure play, you are already behind. The infrastructure war is in full swing, and it will be won by those who secure the 'pipes' before the rest of the market realizes the water has been shut off.

Is your current infrastructure partner building for 2026, or are they just maintaining your 2022 legacy? Audit your compute strategy today.
